description: Observed source limitations and BEACN implementation admission gates; no upstream issue or message was submitted.

issues.observation: The normative datum describes metadata, version and required extra, while displayed JSON examples omit the third field.
issues.consequence: Copying an example can produce a datum that does not satisfy the declared shape.
issues.currentHandling: Use the normative three-field profile in proposed builders; do not treat examples as passing vectors.
issues.acceptanceGate: Serialize and independently decode the chosen datum profile, test missing extra rejection, and obtain target-viewer evidence.

issues.observation: The current document includes nested version-4 metadata in addition to direct versions; its presence is not a wallet support matrix.
issues.consequence: A newly selected version can reduce interoperability even under an Active CIP.
issues.currentHandling: Version-pin each implementation and report unknown consumer support.
issues.acceptanceGate: Exercise exact version-4 fixtures in named consumers before enabling that profile.

issues.observation: CIP-60 prose and v3 CDDL include boolean fields; ordinary transaction metadata does not directly admit JSON booleans. The v3 CDDL also includes conditional expressions that need parser/profile review.
issues.consequence: Naively converting the sample JSON may fail ledger serialization; replacing booleans with strings without disclosure is not demonstrated conformance.
issues.currentHandling: Keep music-profile implementation research-only and omit unsupported optional fields in any narrow experiment.
issues.acceptanceGate: Document a ledger-valid profile, test the selected CDDL/tooling behavior, and verify it with an independent consumer or upstream clarification.

issues.observation: The current README links v3 CDDL and marks v1/v2 deprecated while retaining a heading describing v3 changes as proposed.
issues.consequence: A reader can confuse the parent CIP Active status with a separately proven v3 consumer profile.
issues.currentHandling: Record exact version and this inconsistency; avoid a blanket music-CIP compatibility claim.
issues.acceptanceGate: Version-specific encoding and player acceptance evidence.

issues.observation: CIP-86 prose describes deleting a field by assigning null, which ordinary ledger transaction metadata cannot directly encode.
issues.consequence: A deletion builder needs an agreed valid wire representation rather than a copied JSON null.
issues.currentHandling: Do not ship a deletion profile from the prose alone.
issues.acceptanceGate: Resolve against normative artifacts/upstream and independent reconstruction fixtures.

issues.observation: CIP-86 background describes mint/burn CIP-25 updates, while current CIP-25 constrains metadata updates to positive minting. CIP-86 also names PCRE but later cites ECMAScript regex grammar.
issues.consequence: A reader can accept invalid baseline updates or reconstruct different states across implementations.
issues.currentHandling: Treat CIP-25 positive-mint semantics explicitly; leave regex update support unavailable until a precise bounded profile is tested.
issues.acceptanceGate: Cross-implementation ordered-history fixtures including rollback, invalid baseline events and regex edge cases.

issues.observation: The proposal declares strings objects while later prose/examples discuss externally hosted strings via a URI.
issues.consequence: An implementation that accepts both without an explicit profile may claim more compatibility than its schema proves.
issues.currentHandling: Prioritize a bounded inline-object profile with canonical fallbacks.
issues.acceptanceGate: Confirm exact object/URI representation and test selected viewers; keep externally mutable content visibly distinct.

issues.observation: Current text defines royalty version 2 and numeric postfixes but labels the linked reference implementation as v1, with v2 forthcoming.
issues.consequence: A v1 implementation is insufficient evidence for v2 conformance.
issues.currentHandling: Separate version-1 and version-2 claims and retain experimental status.
issues.acceptanceGate: V2 derivation, selection, rounding and payment fixtures with an independent validator/consumer.

issues.observation: Upstream marks CIP-143 Inactive and incorporated into candidate CIP-0113.
issues.consequence: A copied tooling list can send new implementations toward a retired standalone proposal.
issues.currentHandling: Keep historical entry searchable with explicit inactive reason.
issues.acceptanceGate: Research and pin the candidate replacement independently before implementation.

issues.observation: Canonical proposed v1 uses consumed controlling-asset presence; self-deposit deliberately enables permissionless spending, and historical uniqueness is outside its predicate.
issues.consequence: A generic private-vault UX can make dangerous promises even if it reproduces the canonical validator perfectly.
issues.currentHandling: Limit immediate work to derivation, policy classification and hazard explanation; no funded-vault admission.
issues.acceptanceGate: Canonical vector agreement, adversarial lifecycle/evaluator tests, escrow/cycle analysis and independent security review.

issues.observation: This research reviewed the commitment purpose and structure, not every encryption profile, algorithm registry or conformance vector in the long proposal.
issues.consequence: A minimal digest feature cannot be described as fully CIP-190 compliant or as reviewed cryptography.
issues.currentHandling: Keep a narrow research entry and explicit profile-level admission.
issues.acceptanceGate: Dedicated profile implementation, full vector tests and appropriate cryptographic review.

issues.observation: The latest-release endpoint returned a scalus-uplc workspace package release, not necessarily the principal Lucid package version.
issues.consequence: A repository latest-release tag can install or document the wrong component.
issues.currentHandling: Capture it as an observed release only.
issues.acceptanceGate: Resolve exact package manifest, release and lockfile before adoption.

issues.observation: The latest GitHub release was tagged v0.12.0-beta5 with prerelease false; the README explicitly identifies beta and stable tracks.
issues.consequence: Automating stability decisions from the API boolean misclassifies the release.
issues.currentHandling: Read the maintained node/protocol compatibility table and tag semantics.
issues.acceptanceGate: Choose a tested release/era pair and record that choice.

issues.observation: The examined validateEntry function accepts required-field-complete entries without a native policy; authentication for those entries belongs to another trust layer.
issues.consequence: Using the function alone as issuer verification would confuse structural acceptance with trusted authorship.
issues.currentHandling: Research-only; show the exact trust basis and do not trust a caller-provided verification key by default.
issues.acceptanceGate: Test wrong subject, altered property, stale sequence and untrusted policy-free signer against an explicit trust configuration.

issues.observation: Current inspected peer-connect source uses PeerJS, while the CIP specifies WebTorrent discovery. The dApp verifyConnection hook is optional; the Foundation UI supplies a confirmation callback.
issues.consequence: A CIP label alone does not establish transport interoperability or a complete consent policy.
issues.currentHandling: Research-only; no new wallet connector is enabled by this entry.
issues.acceptanceGate: Pin both peers, define explicit consent and test rejected pairing, account changes, timeouts, disconnect and mobile lifecycle behavior.

issues.observation: The CIP abstract retains two-argument wording, while the normative specification and current V3 evaluator use one ScriptContext containing the redeemer.
issues.consequence: Copying the abstract as the executable interface can construct an incorrect wrapper.
issues.currentHandling: Use the normative V3 interface and pinned implementation definitions; research entry does not promote a new execution receipt.
issues.acceptanceGate: Compare exact handler bytes and versioned hashes, and exercise intended and unintended script-purpose contexts.

issues.observation: The README era table lists Babbage although Conway schema/code exists. The utility imports ajv-formats without listing it in its package manifest; JSON shapes also permit map-order and CBOR-encoding variation.
issues.consequence: The linked code is not established as a clean-install dependency or a byte-canonical commitment codec.
issues.currentHandling: Research-only; preserve original transaction CBOR and body hashes. No upstream installation was attempted.
issues.acceptanceGate: Choose an explicit era/schema profile, resolve dependencies, and test duplicate keys, UTF-8 byte bounds, address semantics and information-preserving display conversion.

issues.observation: Frontend workflow describes JSON/Blake2b hashing; its helper hashes extracted CBOR through Diger. The examined indexer reserializes CBOR with Blake3 and leaves AUTH_END handling unfinished.
issues.consequence: These files do not establish interoperable digest encoding or the full historical authority/revocation lifecycle.
issues.currentHandling: Research-only; no issuer identity or attestation verification feature is enabled.
issues.acceptanceGate: Pin the exact digest preimage and algorithm, label scope, KEL evidence and credential authority at transaction position; test revocation, reauthorization and out-of-order indexing.
